applies_why: The judge text resolves a named link dispute, D5 vs C5, by giving a reason for finding it underdetermined, so K-C's chain-weighing requirement governs it.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'the pressing side's own chain read together' / 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': one reading requires the judge to treat each side's whole chain, including all its footings, as the unit of collision; the other permits splitting the link into wording versus prophetic application and finding no collision when each side addressed a different part.
why: The judge declares the link underdetermined by separating the challenger's wording answer from the defender's application answer, instead of reading each side's chain together and weighing the chains by footing as K-C requires.
